facts.text: Cupertino takes its name from Arroyo San José de Cupertino, a creek christened by Spanish explorer Juan Bautista de Anza’s cartographer after Saint Joseph of Cupertino.
De Anza College occupies a 112‑acre site that once housed the Beaulieu winery, built by Charles and Ella Baldwin at the turn of the 20th century.
Before Silicon Valley’s rise, Cupertino’s economy relied on prunes, apricots, cherries and a 19th‑century winery that marked the area’s agricultural roots.
The Cupertino Historical Society and Museum curates artifacts spanning settlement, agriculture, education, home life and business, keeping the city’s past alive.
Cupertino was officially incorporated in 1955, yet its earliest recorded mention dates back to Spanish exploration in the 18th century.
